summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,000-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best videos are about a robot or a simple sensor trick (gyro, clap switch, PIR motion sensor, IR obstacle avoidance) with a surprising 'it doesn't see/think, it only senses X' angle. Everyday-place videos (lift door, mall door, tap, street light, smoke alarm) and generic 'how does X work?' questions get far fewer views, and the one English video did not reach Instagram at all.
winningPattern: Robot or maker-project subject (robots, clap switch, mic, PIR) + a counterintuitive 'it can't see/hear/think, it only senses X' hook + short Hinglish title with one emoji and #shorts, posted on Instagram first. Titles that state a surprising claim (e.g. 'Taali Nahi, Sirf Shor Sunta Hai', 'Gyro Ke Bina Robot Gir Jaata') beat plain questions ('X Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?'). Robot/Arduino-adjacent topics also earn the most saves and shares, which signal real interest.
doMore: Make robot and maker-project videos: balancing, line follower, obstacle avoidance, clap switch variants
Open with a surprising claim ('X can't see, it only feels Y') instead of a plain question
Post on Instagram first and treat it as the main platform; test YouTube separately with 2-3 titles to find why it lags
End with a save/share prompt like 'Save this for your next Arduino project' since robot IR videos earn the most shares
Keep Hindi narration and Hinglish titles; make follow-ups to the winners (gyro, clap switch, PIR, IR robot)
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' titles on everyday objects like taps, lift doors and mall doors
Near-duplicate topics (smoke detector x2, IR sensor x2, tap x2) posted within days of each other
Posting videos in English or without cross-posting to Instagram
